title: Polynomial-chart pseudo-coherence glues on a principal affine cover
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a finite type morphism of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], and let $m\in\mathbf Z$. Let $X=\bigcup_{\lambda\in I}U_\lambda$ be a covering by principal opens $U_\lambda=D_X(b_\lambda)$, where $b_\lambda\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and $D_X(b_\lambda)$ is the locus where this section is invertible. The index set $I$ is arbitrary. For each $\lambda$, suppose there exist $n_\lambda\geq0$ and a closed immersion $i_\lambda:U_\lambda\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{n_\lambda}_S$ over $S$ for which $R(i_\lambda)_*(E|_{U_\lambda})$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. Then there exist $n\geq0$ and a closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_S$ over $S$ such that $Ri_*E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-nagata-relative-affine-space, def-pc-derived-direct-image, def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Restrictions are derived pullbacks along the open inclusions [def-pc-derived-pullback]. No quasi-coherence assumption on $E$ is imposed.

proof.text: Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact](i), the $b_\lambda$ generate the unit ideal, so choose finitely many of them, denoted $b_1,\ldots,b_r$, and $c_1,\ldots,c_r\in A$ with $\sum_i b_ic_i=1$. These selected principal opens still cover $X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], $A$ has finitely many $R$-algebra generators $a_1,\ldots,a_d$. Put $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_d,y_1,\ldots,y_r,z_1,\ldots,z_r]$, $h=\sum_i y_iz_i-1$, $B=P/(h)$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The map $P\to A$ sending $(x_j,y_i,z_i)$ to $(a_j,b_i,c_i)$ is surjective and kills $h$. Thus [def-weil-closed-immersion] gives closed immersions $k:X\hookrightarrow T$ and $q:T\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}P=\mathbf A^{d+2r}_S$, the last identification being [def-nagata-relative-affine-space]. This also covers $A=0$: one may take the empty finite family, $h=-1$, and $B=0$.

source.place: Tag 09VE, lemma-glue-relative-pseudo-coherent, finite unit relation and the two surjections; Tag 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology; Tag 01T2, lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize

proof.text: Multiplication by $h$ on $P$ is injective: grade by total degree in the $y_i$, and write $v=\sum_{e\geq0}v_e$. If $hv=0$, its degree-zero term gives $v_0=0$ and its degree-$e$ term gives $v_e=(\sum_i y_iz_i)v_{e-1}$, hence all $v_e=0$ by induction. Consequently $0\to P\xrightarrow{h}P\to B\to0$ is exact. Sheafification preserves the kernel by [lem-sc-tilde-preserves-finite-limits] and the cokernel by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](4). By [lem-weil-pbc-pushforward-tilde-spec], the resulting cokernel is $q_*\mathcal O_T$. Thus $[\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}P}\xrightarrow{h}\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}P}]$ in degrees $-1,0$ resolves $(q_*\mathcal O_T)[0]$; it is a bounded finite free model, hence is pseudo-coherent by [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex].

source.place: Tag 09VE, lemma-glue-relative-pseudo-coherent, pseudo-coherence of the auxiliary hypersurface; schemes.tex Tags 01HV, 01I7, 01ID and 01I9

proof.text: Fix $i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}$ and put $W_i=D_T(y_i)$, $U_i=D_X(b_i)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme](0), these are affine with localized coordinate rings, hence are the spectra of $B_{y_i}$ and $A_{b_i}$. Set $C_i=R[x_1,\ldots,x_d,y_1,\ldots,y_r,z_j:j\ne i]$ and $Q_i=C_i[v]$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-linear-equation-localization-polynomial] to the coefficient ring $R[x_1,\ldots,x_d,y_1,\ldots,y_r]$, coefficients $y_j$ and variables $z_j$. It identifies $B_{y_i}$ with $(C_i)_{y_i}$: the retained coordinates are fixed, and $z_i\mapsto y_i^{-1}(1-\sum_{j\ne i}y_jz_j)$. The latter ring is $Q_i/(y_iv-1)$, by the mutually inverse maps $v\mapsto y_i^{-1}$ and $y_i^{-1}\mapsto\bar v$. Thus $r_i:W_i\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}Q_i$ is a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. This uses a Laurent polynomial chart, not the polynomial chart asserted in the last sentence of 09VE's proof.

source.place: Tag 09VE, lemma-glue-relative-pseudo-coherent, the charts W_i; smoothing.tex Tag 07EU, lemma-final-solve, polynomial elimination; explicit correction of the final polynomial-ring assertion

proof.text: Multiplication by $y_iv-1$ on $Q_i$ is injective by comparing degrees in $v$: the constant term of $(y_iv-1)w=0$ gives $w_0=0$, and $w_e=y_iw_{e-1}$ then gives every coefficient zero. Hence $0\to Q_i\xrightarrow{y_iv-1}Q_i\to(C_i)_{y_i}\to0$ is exact. As in step 2, [lem-sc-tilde-preserves-finite-limits] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](4) sheafify this to an exact sequence whose last module is $(r_i)_*\mathcal O_{W_i}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-pushforward-tilde-spec]. Its two-term finite free resolution makes $((r_i)_*\mathcal O_{W_i})[0]$ pseudo-coherent by [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex]. This computation holds over arbitrary $R$, including rings with zero divisors.

source.place: Tag 09VE, lemma-glue-relative-pseudo-coherent, missing Laurent-chart comparison via the hypersurface y_i v - 1; schemes.tex Tags 01HV, 01I7, 01ID and 01I9

proof.text: The induced map $k_i:U_i\to W_i$ comes from the surjection $B_{y_i}\to A_{b_i}$ and is a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its composite $j_i=r_i\circ k_i$ is also a closed immersion directly: $Q_i\to A_{b_i}$ is surjective because $x_j\mapsto a_j$ generate $A$ over $R$ and $v\mapsto b_i^{-1}$ supplies the inverse. Its target is $\mathbf A^{d+2r}_S$ by [def-nagata-relative-affine-space]. The morphism $U_i\to S$ is finite type: its ring is generated over $R$ by $a_1,\ldots,a_d,b_i^{-1}$ (equivalently, local finite type follows from [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], and its affine source is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact]).

source.place: Tag 09VE, lemma-glue-relative-pseudo-coherent, closed embeddings on the local charts; Tag 01T2 and Tag 00E8

proof.text: The hypothesis supplies a polynomial-space embedding of $U_i$ with $m$-pseudo-coherent pushforward of $E|_{U_i}$. By [lem-sfb-affine-polynomial-embedding-pseudocoherence-invariance], applied to the two embeddings of the finite type affine $U_i\to S$, the same holds for $R(j_i)_*(E|_{U_i})$. By [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition] this object is isomorphic to $R(r_i)_*R(k_i)_*(E|_{U_i})$. Isomorphism invariance of $m$-pseudo-coherence follows from [def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex] by composing each approximation with the isomorphism. Step 4 verifies the structure-module hypothesis of [lem-sfb-closed-pushforward-pseudocoherence]; its reverse implication, for the closed immersion $r_i$ and the arbitrary derived object $R(k_i)_*(E|_{U_i})$, now proves this object $m$-pseudo-coherent on $W_i$.

source.place: Tag 09VE, lemma-glue-relative-pseudo-coherent, final local-chart argument corrected using Tag 09VC, lemma-relatively-pseudo-coherent, and perfect.tex Tag 09VA, lemma-closed-push-pseudo-coherent; cohomology.tex Tag 0D5T

proof.text: Put $F=Rk_*E$. The inverse image $k^{-1}(W_i)$ is exactly $U_i$, since $y_i\mapsto b_i$. Therefore [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open] gives $F|_{W_i}\cong R(k_i)_*(E|_{U_i})$, so step 6 proves that $F|_{W_i}$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. The $W_i$ cover $T$: a prime of $B$ containing all the $y_i$ would contain $\sum_i y_iz_i=1$. By [def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex], refine this covering by the local strictly perfect approximations witnessing $m$-pseudo-coherence of each restriction. The resulting approximations witness $m$-pseudo-coherence of $F$ on $T$. Composition of open restrictions is just restriction of complexes (open pullback is exact); equivalently the derived-pullback composition in [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition] identifies their targets. If $r=0$, $T$ is empty and its empty cover gives the same conclusion.

source.place: Tag 09VE, lemma-glue-relative-pseudo-coherent, restriction to the standard cover of T; cohomology.tex Tag 08FE, lemma-restrict-direct-image-open; Tag 08CB, definition-pseudo-coherent

proof.text: The closed immersion $q$ satisfies the structure-module hypothesis by step 2, so the forward implication of [lem-sfb-closed-pushforward-pseudocoherence] gives $m$-pseudo-coherence of $Rq_*F$. By [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition], this is isomorphic to $R(q\circ k)_*E$. The map $q\circ k:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{d+2r}_S$ is a closed immersion because its ring map is the original surjection $P\to A$, by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. It is the required global embedding. Both derived-direct-image lemmas and the closed-pushforward comparison used here apply to arbitrary objects of $D(\mathcal O)$, so no quasi-coherence of $E$ has been introduced.

tool_uses.why: The affine-spectrum unit-ideal and quasi-compactness criterion is a generic algebraic tool for the finite principal subcover, not a replacement for a unit step.
The affine finite-type criterion supplies finitely many algebra generators; no relative-pseudo-coherence theorem is used.
Exactness on kernels for associated module sheaves verifies the explicit two-term hypersurface resolutions.
Preservation of cokernels by the associated-sheaf functor completes these explicit resolutions.
The ordinary affine pushforward formula identifies their cokernels with the actual pushed structure modules.
The affine localization description identifies the selected principal source and ambient opens.
Its explicit elimination formula computes the Laurent polynomial chart in 09VE, without invoking relative pseudo-coherence.
Composition of unbounded derived pushforwards identifies the two successive closed pushforwards.
The unbounded open-restriction comparison identifies F on each W_i with the local closed pushforward.
Composition of open derived restrictions lets the local approximations form one covering witness.
